sections.h2: Where is Dorchester County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Dorchester County sits in the South Carolina Lowcountry and is part of the Charleston metropolitan area. Its county seat is St. George, in the northwest part of the county, while most of the people live in the Summerville and Ladson area to the southeast.

The county covers 571.18 square miles, of which 568.59 are land. It borders Bamberg, Orangeburg, Berkeley, Charleston and Colleton counties. The 2020 census counted 161,540 residents, and the estimate for 2025 is 178,397.

Places named in the county include Summerville, Ladson, North Charleston (partly), Harleyville, Lincolnville, Reevesville, Ridgeville, St. George, Grover, Byrds and Knightsville. Summerville, Ladson and Lincolnville each reach into a neighboring county, so a house near a town line can sit in a different county than its mailing address suggests. Check the parcel's tax map number before you look for a bill.

sections.h2: What is the history of Dorchester County?
sections.html:
The county is young on paper and old on the ground. The General Assembly created it on February 25, 1897, but the first settlement dates to 1696, when Congregationalists settled the area and named it after Dorchester, Massachusetts, their last home.

Summerville began as Pineland Village in 1785, after the Revolutionary War, when plantation owners from the Charleston area settled there to get away from seasonal insects and swamp fever. It became an official town on December 17, 1847. The 1886 Charleston earthquake started a fire that destroyed many buildings on the town square, and the area still lies in the Middleton Place-Summerville seismic zone, the most active in South Carolina.

For a seller, the age mix matters. Older homes near the Summerville Historic District can have different repair needs than a subdivision house built in the last twenty years. Ask your agent or inspector what a buyer is likely to raise.

sections.h2: What drives the Dorchester County economy?
sections.html:
Manufacturing and retail lead. Manufacturing accounts for 15.6 percent of jobs, retail trade 13.4 percent, and accommodation and food services 10.9 percent. The county's 2022 gross domestic product was $5.3 billion, and unemployment ran between 2.6 and 2.9 percent in 2022 and 2023.

As of April 2024 the largest employers were:

  • Bosch
  • Food Lion and Harris Teeter
  • KION Group
  • Publix
  • The town of Summerville
  • Walmart

Summerville also has a medical presence: Summerville Medical Center and several Medical University of South Carolina campuses serve the town.

sections.h2: When are Dorchester County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real property tax is due by January 15, and penalties start the next day. State law makes taxes payable between September 30 and January 15 following the assessment, and the county has mailed bills in mid October in past years. Section 12-45-180 sets the penalty steps, which stack.

After January 153%3%

The county's delinquent page says unpaid bills move to the Delinquent Tax Office after March 16 and carry the 15 percent penalty. State law also says that if title to a property changes during the tax year and the notice went to the prior owner, the treasurer shall waive penalties when the current owner got no timely notice. That is a narrow rule, so do not count on it. If you bought or sold recently, confirm that the bill is going to the right person.

Bills can be paid online through the county's taxes portal, in person at the St. George or Summerville Treasurer's offices, or by mail with the return envelope. If a bill has not arrived by November 10, the Assessor's Office at (843) 832-0162 can verify the mailing address.

sections.h2: Which Dorchester County offices handle which part of the bill?
sections.html:
The Assessor values the property, the Auditor calculates the bill, and the Treasurer collects it. Treat them as three separate stops.

  • Assessor and legal residence: (843) 832-0162, offices in St. George and Summerville. The St. George address is 201 Johnston Street, St. George, SC 29477.
  • Treasurer: led by Cindy Chitty, who collects current property taxes. Questions can go to Treasurer@DorchesterCountySC.gov.
  • Delinquent Tax Office: 201 Johnston Street, St. George, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Phone (843) 563-0110 or (843) 832-0110, email delinquenttax@dorchestercountysc.gov.

The county posts a page on the Treasurer's Office and another on delinquent taxes. Ask each office for a current number before you act, because these pages change.

sections.h2: What happens to a Dorchester County assessment when a house sells?
sections.html:
A sale usually triggers a reappraisal. Under the Property Tax Reform Act of 2006, most transfers count as assessable transfers of interest, and the county reappraises those properties at market value as of December 31 of the year the sale occurred. A buyer's tax bill can therefore differ from yours.

The 4 percent legal residence rate applies to owner-occupied homes, including manufactured homes, and each owner can hold only one. The county asks owners to notify the Assessor within six months of a change in ownership, mailing address or use. Buyers should wait until the deed is recorded with the Register of Deeds before they apply, or the application can be returned.

Mobile homes have their own steps. A mobile home bought in or moved to the county must be registered within 15 days, a moving permit is valid for 30 days, and back taxes must be paid before a permit is issued. A name change permit is needed after an ownership change, and fines of up to $200 may apply. The Assessor's number for that is (843) 832-0162.

Agricultural land has a catch. If the use changes, a rollback of up to three years of tax savings is owed, and the county says it can be charged to whoever changes the use, which may be the new owner. A rollback estimate request form is on the Assessor's site.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Dorchester County assessment?
sections.html:
Put the objection in writing to the county assessor within 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice. That is the rule in Section 12-60-2510 of the South Carolina code, and it applies to disputes over fair market value, special use value, assessment ratio or the assessment itself.

The assessor must send a notice when fair market value rises by $1,000 or more, or when a property is first assessed, normally by July 1. In a countywide reassessment year, notices are due by October 1. If you got no notice, you can still appeal in writing at any time. An appeal filed before the first penalty date applies to that year, and one filed on or after it applies to the next. The county pages we read do not describe its appeal form, so call the Assessor for the current process.

sections.h2: What does collection look like if taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Costs add up in steps. The county's 2025 schedule showed $35 added to real property bills and $45 to mobile home bills by May 12, a $35 posting fee by June 27, and an $80 advertising cost by late October. Card payments carry a 2.95 percent convenience fee.

Personal checks were accepted through September 30, 2025, and the last day to pay taxes was November 14, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. Those are last year's dates, so ask the office for this year's. The county page does not state a redemption period or a sale date, and credit cards cannot be used to redeem property sold at tax sale.

If you are selling a house with delinquent taxes, get a payoff figure from the Delinquent Tax Office, because fees change by date.

sections.h2: What should sellers in Summerville and the rest of Dorchester County expect from the weather?
sections.html:
Expect humidity, heavy rain and the occasional storm. Summerville has a humid subtropical climate with long, hot summers and short, mild winters, average annual precipitation of 52.7 inches, and a record high of 107 degrees Fahrenheit.

Roofs, HVAC systems and crawlspaces take the wear. Buyers who inspect a house will look at those first. Summerville is served by Dorchester School District Two, which runs Summerville High, Ashley Ridge High and Fort Dorchester High, and U.S. Route 78 runs about 24 miles southeast to downtown Charleston, with Interstate 26 crossing the northeast corner of town.

faqs.q: Is Dorchester County property tax due on January 15?
faqs.a: Yes. Real property tax is due by January 15, and a 3 percent penalty begins the next day. A further 7 percent is added after February 1 and 5 percent after March 16, for 15 percent in total.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the 4 percent legal residence rate in Dorchester County?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at (843) 832-0162. Applications can be made online or on paper, and paper forms go to 201 Johnston Street in St. George.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Dorchester County if the property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, but the unpaid tax, penalties and any collection fees have to be cleared. Ask the Delinquent Tax Office for a payoff figure before the closing date and ask your closing agent how it will be paid.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Dorchester County assessment?
faqs.a: State law gives you 90 days from the date the assessor mails the notice. The objection has to be in writing and sent to the assessor.

faqs.q: Does the buyer's tax bill change after a sale?
faqs.a: It can. Most transfers are reappraised at market value as of December 31 of the sale year, so the new owner's bill may differ from yours.
